title: Evel Knievel Part I
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck open Part I of a two-part biography of daredevil Evel Knievel, discussing the Johnny Knoxville documentary, his Butte, Montana childhood, the 1976 Pediatrics "Evel Knievel syndrome" injuries, his early motorcycle racing and crashes, insurance sales, Honda dealership arm-wrestling promotions, his first solo stunt shows and the Barstow crash, and the 1967 Caesars Palace fountain jump that made him a star. The episode ends with a listener mail about ad-break cues and a sign-off teasing Part II.
topics: Success Through a Positive Mental Attitude

entities.name: Success Through a Positive Mental Attitude

segments.title: Opening banter and Johnny Knoxville documentary
segments.summary: Hosts sponsor read for Squarespace, then discuss childhood memories of Evel Knievel toys and the Johnny Knoxville documentary about him.

segments.title: Butte childhood and the 1970s movie
segments.summary: Hosts describe Knievel's rough Butte, Montana upbringing, his grandparents raising him after his parents left, his paper-boy sensationalism, and the George Hamilton film written by John Milius that shaped his public persona.

segments.title: Early life, army, marriage and Butte mining trouble
segments.summary: Knievel was sent to the army instead of prison, then returned to Butte and married Linda Bork, whom he repeatedly cheated on. He was fired from a mining job after a bulldozer wheelie cut power to the city, and was jailed where he met William Knafel, whose nickname inspired the spelling of his name.

segments.title: Hockey exhibition with Czechoslovakian team
segments.summary: Knievel arranged an exhibition hockey game in Montana between the Butte Bombers and the Czechoslovakian national team; afterward the ticket money went missing and he was gone from the venue.

segments.title: Evel Knievel syndrome and injuries from copycat stunts
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the 1976 Pediatrics paper describing the Evel Knievel syndrome, a wave of ER visits by boys injuring themselves imitating his bike jumps, and their own childhood bike stunts.

segments.title: Early racing, insurance sales and Honda dealership promotions
segments.summary: Knievel crashed frequently in motorcycle racing, did not study jump physics, sold insurance well before quitting, and opened a Honda dealership in Moses Lake, Washington, where he used arm-wrestling and stunts like wheelies and firewall jumps to draw customers. He was influenced by W. Clement Stone's self-help book and by meeting Jim Pomeroy.
topics: Success Through a Positive Mental Attitude

segments.title: Solo stunt shows, Barstow crash and car and bus jumps
segments.summary: Inspired by Joey Chitwood, Knievel started his own stunt shows with sponsor Bob Blair, changed his name spelling, and was seriously injured in Barstow attempting a spread-eagle jump. He returned to finish shows and expanded to jumping cars, trucks and buses, crashing often; the hosts compare his jumps unfavorably with modern riders.

segments.title: Caesars Palace fountain jump
segments.summary: In 1967 Knievel decided to jump the Caesars Palace fountains, tricked CEO Jay Sarno with prank calls under different identities, and hired his own film crew, including Lynda Evans, for a jump that ended in a famous crash and sold to ABC, making him a star.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener asks whether Chuck and Josh ever refuse ad-break cues; the hosts answer, plug social channels, and tease Part II.
